ranges.quote: This is episode twenty-two of Exploring Really Cool Tech. Today we'll be talking about webhooks.
ranges.reason: INTRO VARIANT B (cool-tech framing), first take of the shoot and the only complete cool-tech delivery. Acoustic onset 10.50 (ASR 'This' starts 10.48, agreement); acoustic end 14.72 vs ASR 'webhooks.' box end 14.62 -- the voiced tail outlasts the box slightly, end pads 80ms past the acoustic edge.

ranges.quote: So your app finds out you got paid the instant it happens without ever checking. That's called a webhook.
ranges.reason: Only take. Acoustic onset 52.35 (ASR 52.40). ASR boxes 'webhook.' to 56.84; the '-hook' release decays by 56.82 on a 20ms probe, so the range ends 56.98 (+160ms).

ranges.quote: You met the clunky alternative back in the chat episode asking, "Anything new?" on repeat. For payments, that's thousands of wasted calls a day to catch one event.
ranges.reason: Only take; kept as ONE range spanning both phrases -- the 0.51s breath after 'repeat.' (acoustic 68.48-68.99) is natural and under the 0.8s flag line. ASR boxes 'event.' to 72.64 but the release is fully decayed by 72.48 on a 20ms probe (the coarse 0.1s scan read 72.96 off tail noise); end 72.68 = +200ms past the measured decay and still past the ASR box.

ranges.quote: A webhook flips the direction. You hand the payment provider a URL and say, "Call me when something happens."
ranges.reason: Only take. Acoustic onset 74.94 (ASR 'A' starts 75.02); acoustic end 80.64 vs ASR 'happens.' end 80.56. ASR and acoustics agree within a window on both edges.

ranges.quote: The moment a payment succeeds, their server sends an HTTP POST to your URL with the details. You only do work when there's actually work to do,
ranges.reason: First half of one long take (83.22-98.30), split ZERO-GAP from SIGN at 91.39 -- the word boundary between 'do,' (ends 91.37) and 'and' (starts 91.40) -- so each beat gets its own overlay without a cut being audible. Acoustic onset 83.20. The 0.32s breath after 'details.' (88.96-89.28) is natural.

ranges.quote: and because anyone could post to a public URL, they sign each call. You verify the signature so you know it's really them.
ranges.reason: Second half of the same take, contiguous with POST at 91.39 (zero gap by design). ASR boxes 'them.' from 97.14 all the way to 98.30 -- a 1.16s word; find_dead_air puts the acoustic end at 97.34, so the range ends there +100ms. Padding off the ASR box would have shipped ~1s of dead tail.

ranges.quote: So webhooks flip the question. The server calls you. Next, we'll talk about why it only works on my machine is dead.
ranges.reason: FINAL take (of three), preferred per direction and acoustically clean: only a 0.26s breath before 'Next,' (124.16-124.42); the ~0.74s ASR gap there is mostly audible breath, so ONE range spans both phrases. Alternates DROPPED: 99.64 (complete and slightly tighter, but the final delivery is the pick) and 110.70 (aborts mid-word at 'machi-'). ASR boxes 'dead.' from 127.62 to 129.60 -- a 1.98s word; acoustic end is 128.00, range ends there +100ms. Acoustic onset 121.41 vs ASR 'So' start 121.48.

_zoom_note: Slow FACE-ANCHORED zoom, focal (540,730) = eye line, magnitude 1.08, direction alternating so the drift is continuous across cuts. Rebuilt 2026-08-28 per feedback ('zoom shakes, make it stronger'): render.py's zoom chain is now supersampled with the crop offset derived from the frame's actual quantized size, killing the size/offset rounding mismatch that caused the judder; magnitude raised 1.045->1.08 and focal moved from frame centre to the eye line so the stronger zoom displaces the face far less against overlay clearances.
_windows_note: Output-timeline windows on render.py's real 24fps extract grid: each segment's rendered duration is ceil((end-start)*24)/24, not the raw source span. Verified against rendered clips where measurable. Overlay start_in_output values are derived from THESE numbers.
